purpose: Discovery-only registry of reusable or potentially reusable intelligence across the National Tools network.

principles: A new tool should check the registry when an existing engine may answer part of its problem.
Finding a candidate engine never creates an obligation to use it.
Reuse only when the engine's inputs, outputs, source semantics, geographic validity and uncertainty model fit the new tool.
A tool may use one engine, several engines, or none.
Never distort a product, user experience, scientific model or source choice merely to reuse existing code.
Prefer composition over copying when a stable package or HTTP contract already exists.
Do not create cross-repository coupling to internal files without an explicit versioned contract.
Tool-specific formulas remain tool-specific unless deliberately generalized, tested and versioned.
Pattern reuse is not formula reuse: biology- or destination-specific weights must not be transplanted into a different domain without independent validation.
If a cleaner new engine is warranted, build it and add it to the registry after validation.
decisionQuestions: Does an existing engine answer a real sub-question this tool needs?
Are its source semantics and geographic coverage valid here?
Would reuse reduce duplication without reducing product quality?
Is there a stable package or HTTP contract, or would reuse create brittle coupling?
Would a new purpose-built implementation be clearer, safer or more accurate?

reuseClasses.shared-contract: Already designed for cross-tool use through a stable shared package or contract.
reuseClasses.proven-engine: A working decision/data engine in an owning repo that may be consumed through a stable API or deliberately extracted later.
reuseClasses.extractable-component: Contains generally useful logic, but it is currently embedded in a tool and should not be imported directly across repos.
reuseClasses.pattern-reference: Useful architecture or modeling pattern; formulas/weights remain domain-specific and should not be reused verbatim.
reuseClasses.tool-specific: Keep local unless a future use case justifies generalization.

engines.name: National Outdoor Core
useWhen: a new tool needs already-standardized cross-tool infrastructure
avoidWhen: the logic is domain-specific and does not belong in shared infrastructure
engines.notes: This is infrastructure, not a mandate to route every decision through a common engine.

engines.name: River State & Context
avoidWhen: an exact local hydrology source is materially better
the tool would turn river state into an unsupported safety or fish-bite claim
engines.notes: Strong reuse candidate; owner retains river semantics and source lifecycle.

engines.name: Aurora Visibility
avoidWhen: a product only needs generic darkness/cloud data
the new use would treat Kp or OVATION as a guaranteed sighting probability
engines.notes: Already consumes shared helpers from national-outdoor-core.

engines.name: Coastal Water Window
avoidWhen: freshwater or inland logic needs materially different sources
reuse would override official beach-risk wording
engines.notes: Use as a coastal signal, not as a universal water-safety engine.

engines.name: Snowpack & Melt
avoidWhen: the tool needs avalanche, groomed-trail, road-access or ice-safety conclusions
engines.notes: Measured-pack distance rules and prohibited claims remain part of the engine contract.

engines.name: Frost & Freeze Timing
avoidWhen: hardiness zone alone is being substituted for actual frost climatology
engines.notes: Planting may consume frost outputs, but planting rules remain a separate domain layer.

engines.name: Planting Calendar
answers: crop planting windows derived from frost timing and crop-specific rules
avoidWhen: the target crop/location needs a different extension-backed rule set
engines.notes: Do not force planting logic into unrelated garden products.

engines.name: Garden Water Stress
avoidWhen: soil/plant-specific certainty cannot be supported
engines.notes: Conservative context engine, not an automatic irrigation controller.

engines.name: White Christmas Intelligence
possibleConsumers: holiday snow planning where semantics match exactly
avoidWhen: generic snow probability or winter weather tools
engines.notes: Narrow seasonal semantics; do not generalize casually.

engines.name: Cumberland Moonbow Observation Engine
possibleConsumers: future lunar-phenomenon tools after extracting only genuinely generic components
avoidWhen: a new tool would copy Cumberland-specific thresholds or geometry
engines.notes: Astronomy/confidence patterns may generalize; moonbow score itself is destination-specific.

engines.name: Yosemite Firefall Observation Engine
avoidWhen: the target does not share Horsetail's geometry/runoff physics
reuse would copy Firefall weights without validation
engines.notes: Solar, clarity and trip-window components are candidates for later generalization; the Firefall probability model remains local.

engines.name: Monarch Migration Model
possibleConsumers: future insect migration models after independent validation
avoidWhen: birds, cranes or other species with different biology
copying weights or latitude tables verbatim
engines.notes: Reuse the modeling pattern, not the monarch-specific model.

engines.name: Rocky Mountain Elk Rut Viewing Model
possibleConsumers: other elk regions after region-specific validation
avoidWhen: other species
other elk populations without validating timing/access rules
copying RMNP closures or weights into another destination
engines.notes: Pattern reference unless/until a generalized wildlife-window engine is deliberately created.

registrationRule: Add an entry when an engine or component has demonstrated reusable value. Registration documents availability; it does not require adoption by any present or future tool.
extractionRule: Do not move working code merely because it appears in this registry. Extract only when a real second consumer exists and the generalized contract can be tested without weakening the owning tool.
